tools.name: get-decompilation
tools.title: Get Function Decompilation

Defaults to 50 lines to conserve context - start with small chunks (10-20 lines) then expand as needed using offset/limit. Updating variable data types and names can significantly improve decompilation quality. Use includeCallers/includeCallees to get caller/callee lists in one call (avoids separate tool invocations).

functionNameOrAddress.description: Function name, address, or symbol to decompile (e.g. 'main', '0x00401000', or 'start'). For addresses pointing inside a function, the containing function will be decompiled.

includeCallers.description: Include list of functions that call this one (name, address, signature). Use for understanding function usage without bulk decompilation.

programPath.description: Path in the Ghidra Project to the program containing the function

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-based). Defaults to 1.

includeDisassembly.description: Whether to include assembly listing alongside decompilation for sync

includeIncomingReferences.description: Whether to include incoming cross references to this function on the function declaration line

limit.description: Number of lines to return. Defaults to 50 lines to conserve context. Use smaller chunks (10-20 lines) for initial exploration, then expand as needed.

includeReferenceContext.description: Whether to include code context snippets from calling functions (requires includeIncomingReferences)

includeComments.description: Whether to include comments in the decompilation output

includeCallees.description: Include list of functions this one calls (name, address, signature). Use for understanding function dependencies without bulk decompilation.

signatureOnly.description: Return only signature/metadata without decompiled code. Saves output tokens.

tools.name: analyze-program
tools.title: Analyze Program
tools.description: Run Ghidra's auto-analysis on a program as a background job, then persist the result. Waits inline up to waitSeconds for completion: small programs finish in that window and return the full result (success, analyzersRun, durationMs, persisted, saved, ...) in one call with status=completed. Longer analyses return {status:running, jobId, log} so you can poll analysis-status with the jobId (or stop it with analysis-cancel). Only one analysis runs per program at a time — calling again while one is in flight reuses the running job. Supports per-call analyzer overrides via enableAnalyzers / disableAnalyzers (use list-analyzers for valid names) and a persist mode (auto/save/none). After import-file, call this tool to populate functions, strings, and references.

forceFullAnalysis.description: Force a full re-analysis even if the program is already marked analyzed (default: false). When false, the first call on a fresh program runs full analysis and subsequent calls are incremental.

programPath.description: Path to the program to analyze (e.g., '/Hatchery.exe')

disableAnalyzers.description: Names of analyzers to disable for this run only (does not persist). Each name must be a top-level analyzer enable flag (no dots in the name) -- use list-analyzers to discover valid names.

waitSeconds.description: Seconds to wait inline for analysis to finish before returning a job handle to poll. Small programs finish within this window and return the full result in one call; long analyses return {status:running, jobId} to poll with analysis-status. Keep this safely below your MCP client's tool-call timeout — the inline wait holds the request open, so a value above the client timeout would drop the call (the job still runs and stays pollable).

timeoutSeconds.description: Maximum analysis time in seconds. Defaults to the configured analysis timeout. Pass -1 to disable the timeout entirely (analysis runs until done).

persist.description: How to persist the analysis when it finishes: auto = save locally then checkin if the file is under version control; save = local save only; none = don't persist (read-only).

enableAnalyzers.description: Names of analyzers to enable for this run only (does not persist). Each name must be a top-level analyzer enable flag (no dots in the name) -- use list-analyzers to discover valid names.

tools.name: analysis-status
tools.title: Analysis Status
tools.description: Poll a background analysis job started by analyze-program. Call repeatedly, feeding back logCursor as sinceLogSeq, until status is terminal (completed/failed/cancelled/timed_out). Each call returns the new log lines since the cursor and the live function count, and long-polls up to waitSeconds for progress — returning immediately when the job finishes. When terminal, the response also carries the full result (persisted, saved, durationMs, ...). Identify the job by jobId (preferred) or by programPath (resolves to that program's latest job).

jobId.description: The analysis job to poll (e.g., 'analysis-3'), as returned by analyze-program. Provide exactly one of jobId or programPath.

programPath.description: Alternative to jobId: the program path (e.g., '/Hatchery.exe') whose LATEST analysis job should be polled. Provide exactly one of jobId or programPath.

waitSeconds.description: Seconds to long-poll: the call holds open up to this long waiting for progress, then returns. It returns the instant the job terminates. Keep this safely below your MCP client's tool-call timeout — the inline wait holds the request open, so a value above the client timeout would drop the call (the job still runs and stays pollable).

maxLogEntries.description: Maximum number of log entries to return per call. When more are available, truncated is true and you should call again with sinceLogSeq=logCursor to drain them.

sinceLogSeq.description: Return only log entries with seq greater than this cursor. Feed back the previous call's logCursor here to get just the new lines.

tools.name: analysis-cancel
tools.title: Analysis Cancel
tools.description: Request cancellation of a running background analysis job started by analyze-program. Cancellation is asynchronous: this returns immediately after requesting it; poll analysis-status until the job reaches a terminal state (cancelled) to confirm. Partial analysis work is still persisted when the job unwinds. If the job has already finished, this is a no-op and reports alreadyTerminal:true.

tools.name: import-file

tools.description: Import files, directories, or archives into the Ghidra project using batch import. Set analyzeAfterImport=true to bundle analysis into the import call (slower, no per-analyzer progress).

analyzeAfterImport.description: Run auto-analysis on each imported program before returning (default: false). Prefer leaving this off for LLM-driven workflows and calling analyze-program explicitly so progress is reported and analyzer choices are visible.

functionAddress.description: Address or name of the function to search for in vtables

tools.name: diff-create-session
tools.title: Create Binary Diff Session
tools.description: Correlate two programs with Ghidra Version Tracking and cache the result as a background job. Waits inline up to waitSeconds (default 10): small binaries finish in that window and return the full summary; large binaries return {status:running, jobId} to poll via diff-status. Idempotent unless force=true or the correlators selection changes. Both programs must already be analyzed. NOTE: if a correlation for this same pair is already running, this call attaches to that in-flight job and the force/correlators overrides on this call are ignored until it finishes. Returns summary counts and the correlators that ran.

sourceProgramPath.description: Project path of the trusted/analyzed/old program (markup flows FROM here).

waitSeconds.description: Seconds to wait inline for correlation to finish before returning a job handle. Small binaries finish in this window and return the full summary; large ones return {status:running, jobId} to poll via diff-status. Keep below your MCP client tool-call timeout.

destinationProgramPath.description: Project path of the variant/new/patched program (markup flows TO here; changes are relative to source).

timeoutSeconds.description: Hard cap on correlation time in seconds; -1 (default) for unlimited.

force.description: Re-correlate even if a session already exists for this pair.

sourceScope.description: Optional: restrict the initial correlation to these source functions (names or addresses). Omitted = all functions, then auto-scoped to the residual per stage.

correlators.description: Ordered VT correlators to run. Omit for the default sequence: [symbol-name, exact-bytes, exact-instructions, exact-mnemonics, duplicate-instructions, function-reference]. Drop 'symbol-name' to match by structure/bytes instead of trusting symbol names (e.g. when names are stripped, unreliable, or you want a body-based diff that surfaces decompilation changes). 'combined-reference' is an opt-in reference-based correlator (not in the default sequence) that can match functions across body changes when their call/data references are stable — useful for stripped binaries; caveat: leaf functions with no references still won't match (Ghidra VT has no body-similarity correlator). Changing the selection re-correlates this pair.

destinationScope.description: Optional: restrict the initial correlation to these destination functions (names or addresses). Omitted = all functions.

tools.name: diff-add-correlator
tools.title: Refine Diff With Another Correlator
tools.description: Run one more VT correlator over the existing session's still-unmatched residual (or an agent-chosen scope) and persist. The refine step: correlate broadly with diff-create-session, read the residual (diff-list-functions category=removed/added), then aim a sharper correlator at a chosen subset. Runs as a background job.

sourceProgramPath.description: Project path of the trusted/analyzed/old program (markup flows FROM here).

correlator.description: Which correlator to run over the residual (or chosen scope).

waitSeconds.description: Seconds to wait inline before returning a {status:running, jobId}.

destinationProgramPath.description: Project path of the variant/new/patched program (markup flows TO here; changes are relative to source).

sourceScope.description: Optional source functions (names/addresses) to scope this correlator to. Omitted = the current unmatched residual.

destinationScope.description: Optional destination functions to scope this correlator to. Omitted = residual.

tools.name: diff-summary
tools.title: Binary Diff Summary
tools.description: Counts plus a ranked teaser of the most-changed matched functions, each tagged with a changeTypes profile (similarity/callees/size, plus body-bytes when includeBodyByteChanges=true). The 'what changed?' entry point.

sourceProgramPath.description: Project path of the trusted/analyzed/old program (markup flows FROM here).

destinationProgramPath.description: Project path of the variant/new/patched program (markup flows TO here; changes are relative to source).

includeBodyByteChanges.description: Recall knob (default false). Also flag matched functions whose raw instruction bytes differ — catches operand/control-flow tweaks that VT scores as identical (changeType 'body-bytes'). Precise on relocatable objects (.ko); noisy on fully-linked images where unchanged functions shift, so the agent enables it deliberately and filters the residual.

topN.description: How many most-changed matched functions to include in the teaser.

tools.name: diff-list-functions
tools.title: List Diffed Functions
tools.description: Paginated list of function diff rows for one category (changed/added/removed/identical). Each matched row carries a changeTypes profile (similarity/callees/size, plus body-bytes when includeBodyByteChanges=true), sizeDelta, and any calleeChanges — no bodies.

sourceProgramPath.description: Project path of the trusted/analyzed/old program (markup flows FROM here).

destinationProgramPath.description: Project path of the variant/new/patched program (markup flows TO here; changes are relative to source).

includeBodyByteChanges.description: Recall knob (default false). Also treat matched functions whose raw instruction bytes differ as changed (changeType 'body-bytes') — catches operand/control-flow tweaks VT scores as identical. Precise on .ko; noisy on linked images. Affects which rows land in the changed vs identical category.

tools.name: diff-function
tools.title: Diff One Function Pair
tools.description: Side-by-side decompiler diff for one matched function pair: changed-line snippets, similarity, matching correlator, and both signatures.

sourceProgramPath.description: Project path of the trusted/analyzed/old program (markup flows FROM here).

includeArtifactHunks.description: Show decompiler-artifact hunks (variable renumbering, string-label content) in full instead of collapsing them. Default false — artifacts are tagged and counted under suppressedHunks but their content is omitted.

function.description: Function name or address on EITHER side; the matched counterpart is resolved via the session.

destinationProgramPath.description: Project path of the variant/new/patched program (markup flows TO here; changes are relative to source).

tools.name: diff-strings
tools.title: Diff Strings
tools.description: Added/removed defined strings between source and destination. Signal for signature updates and C2/protocol changes.

sourceProgramPath.description: Project path of the trusted/analyzed/old program (markup flows FROM here).

destinationProgramPath.description: Project path of the variant/new/patched program (markup flows TO here; changes are relative to source).

tools.name: diff-data
tools.title: Diff Defined Data
tools.description: Added/removed defined data (by representation + address) between source and destination.

sourceProgramPath.description: Project path of the trusted/analyzed/old program (markup flows FROM here).

destinationProgramPath.description: Project path of the variant/new/patched program (markup flows TO here; changes are relative to source).

tools.name: diff-transfer-markup
tools.title: Transfer Analysis Markup
tools.description: Auto-apply VT markup (names/prototypes/datatypes/comments) from source to destination for matches at/above the confidence floor, in a transaction. Returns applied matches and the below-floor proposals for selective review. Runs as a background job: waits inline up to waitSeconds, then returns {status:running, jobId} for large match sets.

sourceProgramPath.description: Project path of the trusted/analyzed/old program (markup flows FROM here).

confidence.description: Similarity floor for auto-apply (0..1). Matches below are returned as proposals.

waitSeconds.description: Seconds to wait inline for the transfer to finish before returning a job handle. Small match sets finish in this window; large-image transfers return {status:running, jobId} to poll via diff-status.

destinationProgramPath.description: Project path of the variant/new/patched program (markup flows TO here; changes are relative to source).

tools.name: diff-apply-match
tools.title: Apply One Diff Match
tools.description: Apply VT markup for exactly one matched function pair (a proposal the agent chose). Mutates the destination program in a transaction.

sourceProgramPath.description: Project path of the trusted/analyzed/old program (markup flows FROM here).

sourceAddress.description: Source function address of the match to apply.

destinationAddress.description: Destination function address of the match to apply.

destinationProgramPath.description: Project path of the variant/new/patched program (markup flows TO here; changes are relative to source).

tools.name: diff-list-sessions
tools.title: List Diff Sessions
tools.description: List persisted diff sessions (kept durably until explicitly deleted): each source/destination pair and the correlators run so far.

tools.name: diff-delete-session
tools.title: Delete Diff Session
tools.description: Permanently delete a persisted diff session (its Version Tracking DomainFile). This is the only thing that removes a session — sessions are never auto-deleted; the next diff-create-session for the pair re-correlates fresh.

sourceProgramPath.description: Project path of the trusted/analyzed/old program (markup flows FROM here).

destinationProgramPath.description: Project path of the variant/new/patched program (markup flows TO here; changes are relative to source).

tools.name: diff-status
tools.title: Poll Diff Job
tools.description: Poll a background diff job (correlation or markup transfer) started by diff-create-session / diff-transfer-markup. Returns new log lines since the cursor and, when terminal, the full result (the summary, or the applied/proposed markup). Identify by jobId, or by the source+destination pair (resolves to the latest job).

sourceProgramPath.description: Project path of the trusted/analyzed/old program (markup flows FROM here).

jobId.description: The diff job to poll (e.g. 'diff-3'), as returned by diff-create-session or diff-transfer-markup. Provide jobId, or the source+destination pair.

waitSeconds.description: Seconds to long-poll; returns the instant the job terminates. Keep below your MCP client tool-call timeout.

destinationProgramPath.description: Project path of the variant/new/patched program (markup flows TO here; changes are relative to source).

maxLogEntries.description: Max log entries per call; drain more with sinceLogSeq=logCursor.

sinceLogSeq.description: Return only log entries with seq greater than this cursor (feed back the previous logCursor).

tools.name: diff-cancel
tools.title: Cancel Diff Job
tools.description: Request cancellation of a running diff job started by diff-create-session or diff-transfer-markup. Asynchronous: poll diff-status until status is cancelled. A cancelled markup transfer rolls back (all-or-nothing).

tools.name: set-comment

tools.description: Set or update a comment at a specific address. Use this to keep notes or annotations for yourself and the human.

programPath.description: Path in the Ghidra Project to the program

addressOrSymbol.description: Address or symbol name where to set the comment

tools.name: run-script
tools.title: Run Python Script
tools.description: Execute a Python script in the Ghidra PyGhidra runtime against a specific program. Requires Ghidra to be launched via PyGhidra (mcp-reva or pyghidra-gui). Returns captured stdout/stderr, duration, and timeout flag. Script failures appear in stderr with success=false; tool failures (bad args, PyGhidra unavailable) are MCP errors. Cancellation is cooperative: long-running scripts should periodically check monitor.isCancelled() so the timeout can fire on tight loops.

scriptPath.description: Absolute path to an existing .py script to run.

programPath.description: Path to the program in the Ghidra Project

code.description: Inline Python source. The script runs as a Ghidra script with currentProgram, FlatProgramAPI helpers, and monitor available. Wrap state changes in currentProgram.startTransaction(...) / endTransaction(...) yourself — the tool does not open a transaction. Provide exactly one of: code, scriptPath, scriptName.

scriptName.description: Name of a script (e.g., 'MyAnalysis.py') resolved across registered Ghidra script directories.

timeoutSeconds.description: Per-call timeout override in seconds. Defaults to the configured script timeout.

tools.name: list-scripts
tools.title: List Scripts
tools.description: List Python scripts visible to Ghidra across all registered script directories (user dir + system dirs + bundle dirs). Filterable by path or name; supports pagination.

pathFilter.description: Optional substring filter on script absolute path

nameFilter.description: Optional substring filter on script file name

tools.name: read-script
tools.title: Read Script
tools.description: Read a script's source, returned with cat -n style line numbers so you can reference exact lines in edit-script. Supports chunked reads via offset/limit. Sets truncated=true if more lines remain.

scriptPath.description: Absolute path to the script. Provide either scriptPath or scriptName.

scriptName.description: Script file name resolved across registered script directories.

tools.name: write-script
tools.title: Write Script
tools.description: Create a new script or fully replace an existing one in a writeable script directory. System directories are read-only. Use edit-script for targeted changes instead of full rewrites.

scriptPath.description: Absolute path; must resolve under a writeable script directory.

scriptName.description: File name (e.g., 'MyAnalysis.py') — written to the default writeable scripts directory.

overwrite.description: Overwrite existing file. Default false: errors if file exists.

tools.name: edit-script
tools.title: Edit Script
tools.description: Replace exact old_string with new_string in a script. Errors if old_string isn't found, or if it matches multiple locations and replace_all is false. Use this instead of write-script when iterating on an existing script.

scriptPath.description: Absolute path to the script to edit (must be writeable).

old_string.description: Exact text to find. Must occur exactly once unless replace_all is true; surround with enough context to make it unique.

scriptName.description: Script file name resolved under the default writeable scripts directory.

replace_all.description: Replace every occurrence. Default false: errors if old_string matches more than one location.

new_string.description: Replacement text. Must differ from old_string.
